name: Rapidly Involuting Congenital Hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Hemangiomas

criteria.description: Presence of a fully formed vascular tumor at birth
Complete or near-complete involution of the lesion within the first 12 to 18 months of life
Characteristic imaging findings on ultrasound or MRI showing high-flow vascular lesion with no postnatal growth
Lack of proliferative phase typical of infantile hemangiomas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a congenital vascular lesion with characteristic imaging features and documented rapid involution within 12-18 months
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology may be used to confirm diagnosis but is not routinely required.

laboratory: Normal or mild thrombocytopenia in some cases
Coagulation profile usually normal unless Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon present
imaging: Ultrasound: high-flow vascular lesion with arterial and venous signals
MRI: well-circumscribed lesion with flow voids, no postnatal growth
Absence of proliferative phase typical of infantile hemangiomas
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathology shows lobular capillary proliferation with large abnormal vessels
Immunohistochemistry negative for GLUT-1 (distinguishes from infantile hemangioma)

distinguishingFeatures: Similar congenital presentation but persistent lesion

redFlags: Coagulopathy or thrombocytopenia suggestive of Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon
references: Drolet BA, et al. Congenital hemangiomas: clinical and histopathologic features. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2008.
Haggstrom AN, et al. Prospective study of congenital hemangiomas: clinical features and natural history. Pediatrics. 2010.
